Range Lands
Revegetation of the mined area is to be conducted in accordance with the reclamation laws of the State of Montana and the conditions of the lease. Westmoreland Resources contemplates grazing trials as part of the reclamation process, as well as revegetation monitoring. Most rangeland in the area is in fair condition due to past and present grazing practices. Because reclamation is expected to result in an improved species composition, forage production will likely increase over pre-mining conditions. However, this cannot be supported until experience is gained in actual reclamation.
For detailed discussion of the reclamation plan, see Chapter I of this statement.
Timber
Planting of trees and shrubs will be accomplished concurrently with other revegetation projects.
Initial research data indicates that reclamation of strip mined lands is possible. However, only time will tell if these initial revegetation efforts will be conducive to the establishment of a stable plant community. Richard Hodder of Montana State University stated (oral communications, 1/23/1976) that research data shows that preliminary reforestation attempts on non-forest mining sites in Southeastern Montana have been successful and that re-establishing forest cover on mining sites located in a forest environment (such as the Project Area) should be quite successful. This conclusion remains to be verified on the project site.
